name: Quest: Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: Long-context decode is slow mainly because attention must read the whole KV cache from HBM, and prior KV-selection work assumed token criticality is query-INDEPENDENT, when in fact which tokens matter depends on the current query.
mechanism: Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference. Partition the KV cache into fixed-size pages and track, per page, only the MINIMUM and MAXIMUM key values. At decode time, use the query vector to compute an UPPER BOUND on each page's criticality from those two extrema (the bound is exact-criticality-safe by construction) and load only the Top-K pages for attention. Selects pages, not tokens, so the loads stay aligned and coalesced.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): up to 2.23x SELF-ATTENTION speedup, which reduces INFERENCE LATENCY by up to 7.03x, with negligible accuracy loss on long-dependency tasks. The two numbers measure different things and the gap between them is the interesting part - the 7.03x end-to-end latency reduction exceeds the 2.23x kernel speedup because loading fewer pages also shrinks the memory-hierarchy pressure outside attention. Never quote the 7.03x without the 2.23x.
